typedef struct TMTag
{
	char *name; /**< Name of tag */
	TMTagType type; /**< Tag Type */
	gint refcount; /* the reference count of the tag */

	/** These are tag attributes */
	TMSourceFile *file; /**< File in which the tag occurs; NULL for global tags */
	gulong line; /**< Line number of the tag */
	gboolean local; /**< Is the tag of local scope */
	guint flags; /**< Additional flags */
	char *arglist; /**< Argument list (functions/prototypes/macros) */
	char *scope; /**< Scope of tag */
	char *inheritance; /**< Parent classes */
	char *var_type; /**< Variable type (maps to struct for typedefs) */
	char access; /**< Access type (public/protected/private/etc.) */
	char impl; /**< Implementation (e.g. virtual) */
	TMParserType lang; /* Programming language of the file */
	gchar kind_letter; /* Kind letter from ctags */
} TMTag;
objects.description: Represents a single tag discovered by the tag manager. Stores identifying data (name, type), source location (file, line), semantic attributes (scope, inheritance, arglist, var_type), and metadata (access, impl, flags, language, kind letter). TMTag instances are reference-counted; they are typically constructed and owned by TMSourceFile during parsing, and tag operations manipulate arrays of TMTag pointers without modifying the objects themselves.

Singleton Tag Manager workspace object holding project-wide state: arrays of global tags, per-source-file objects, and aggregated/sorted tag views used for autocomplete, calltips, and syntax highlighting. Members are GLib containers storing pointers to TMTag and TMSourceFile objects; ownership of tag objects typically remains with their source files. source_file_map accelerates lookups by filename. Construction is implicitly managed by the internal workspace accessors; users add/remove TMSourceFile instances via the provided API. Destruction is via tm_workspace_free when available under GEANY_PRIVATE builds. Some details (lifecycle and thread-safety) are not documented here and may depend on the wider Tag Manager subsystem.

functions.description: Finds an open document by its UTF-8 filename (GeanyDocument::file_name). Returns the matching document or NULL if not found.
requirements: utf8_filename must be UTF-8 encoded.
utf8_filename should match the document's UTF-8 filename as stored in GeanyDocument::file_name.

functions.name: document_find_by_real_path
functions.description: Finds an open document by its real, link-dereferenced, locale-encoded filesystem path (GeanyDocument::real_path). Returns the matching document or NULL if not found.
requirements: realname must be locale-encoded (consistent with GeanyDocument::real_path).
realname should be the link-dereferenced absolute path used for on-disk identity.

functions.name: document_save_file
functions.description: Saves the given document to its current filename. Returns TRUE on success, FALSE on failure. Set force to save even if the document is not marked as changed.
requirements: doc must be non-NULL and refer to a valid, open GeanyDocument.
The document must have or be able to determine a target filename for saving.

functions.name: document_open_file
functions.signature: GeanyDocument* document_open_file(const gchar *locale_filename, gboolean readonly, GeanyFiletype *ft, const gchar *forced_enc);
functions.description: Opens a file into a new document. The filename must be in the system locale encoding. Optionally opens as read-only, sets an initial filetype, and/or forces a specific text encoding. Returns the created document or NULL on failure.
requirements: locale_filename must be a valid, existing path encoded in the system locale.
If readonly is TRUE, the document will be read-only.
If provided, ft must be a valid GeanyFiletype pointer (reference to an existing filetype).
If provided, forced_enc must be a valid encoding name string.

functions.name: document_open_files
functions.signature: void document_open_files(const GSList *filenames, gboolean readonly, GeanyFiletype *ft, const gchar *forced_enc);
functions.description: Opens multiple files into documents. The list should contain filename strings. Optionally opens them read-only, sets an initial filetype, and/or forces a text encoding for all. Non-void; failures for individual files are handled internally.
requirements: filenames must be a valid GSList; each list node’s data should be a filename string pointer.
Filename string encoding is expected to match what document_open_file accepts (typically system locale).
If readonly is TRUE, opened documents will be read-only.
If provided, ft must be a valid GeanyFiletype pointer (reference to an existing filetype).
If provided, forced_enc must be a valid encoding name string.

functions.name: document_remove_page
functions.description: Closes/removes the document at the given notebook page index. Returns TRUE on success, FALSE if the page is invalid or removal failed.
requirements: page_num must refer to an existing notebook page index.

functions.name: document_reload_force
functions.description: Reloads the document content from disk, forcing a reload even if unchanged. Optionally specifies a text encoding to use. Returns TRUE on success, FALSE on failure.
requirements: doc must be non-NULL and refer to a valid, open GeanyDocument.
If provided, forced_enc must be a valid encoding name string.

functions.name: document_set_encoding
functions.description: Sets the document’s text encoding to the specified encoding name. Use to update the document’s encoding metadata and related behavior.
requirements: doc must be non-NULL and refer to a valid, open GeanyDocument.
new_encoding must be a valid string representation of an encoding (per encodings_get_charset_from_index).

functions.name: document_set_text_changed
functions.description: Marks the document’s changed/dirty state. Use to programmatically set whether the document is considered modified since last save.
requirements: doc must be non-NULL and refer to a valid, open GeanyDocument.

functions.name: document_set_filetype
functions.description: Sets the document’s filetype. Affects syntax highlighting, indentation, and other filetype-specific behaviors.
requirements: doc must be non-NULL and refer to a valid, open GeanyDocument.
type must be a valid GeanyFiletype pointer; it should be a reference to one of the elements of the global filetypes array (as per GeanyDocument::file_type documentation).

functions.name: document_close
functions.description: Closes the given document. Returns TRUE on success, FALSE if closing was canceled or failed.
requirements: doc must be non-NULL and refer to a valid, open GeanyDocument.

functions.name: document_index
functions.description: Returns the document at the given document array index, or NULL if the index is invalid. Provides random access to open documents.
requirements: idx must be within the valid range of open document indices.

functions.name: document_save_file_as
functions.description: Saves the document to a new UTF-8 filename (Save As). Returns TRUE on success, FALSE on failure.
requirements: doc must be non-NULL and refer to a valid, open GeanyDocument.
utf8_fname must be UTF-8 encoded.

functions.name: document_rename_file
functions.description: Updates the document’s filename to a new name. Use after an external rename or to change the display name associated with the document.
requirements: doc must be non-NULL and refer to a valid, open GeanyDocument.
new_filename should be UTF-8 encoded (consistent with GeanyDocument::file_name).

functions.name: document_get_status_color
functions.description: Returns a GdkColor representing the document’s status (e.g., modified, read-only) for UI display, or NULL if unavailable.
requirements: doc must be non-NULL and refer to a valid, open GeanyDocument.

functions.name: document_get_basename_for_display
functions.description: Returns a string containing the document’s base filename formatted for display, possibly truncated to the given length. Ownership/cleanup of the returned string is unknown from this header; consult implementation or API docs.
requirements: doc must be non-NULL and refer to a valid, open GeanyDocument.
length specifies the display length constraint; exact semantics are not documented here.

functions.name: document_get_notebook_page
functions.description: Returns the notebook page index for the given document, or a negative value on error. Use to find the tab position of a document.
requirements: doc must be non-NULL and refer to a valid, open GeanyDocument.

functions.name: document_compare_by_display_name
functions.description: Comparator function to order documents by their display name. Suitable for use with GLib sorting APIs; returns negative/zero/positive as a is less than/equal to/greater than b.
requirements: a and b must point to GeanyDocument* (or pointers to such) as expected by the caller’s container/iteration context.

functions.name: document_compare_by_tab_order
functions.description: Comparator function to order documents by their tab order (left-to-right). Suitable for use with GLib sorting APIs; returns negative/zero/positive as a is less than/equal to/greater than b.
requirements: a and b must point to GeanyDocument* (or pointers to such) as expected by the caller’s container/iteration context.

functions.name: document_compare_by_tab_order_reverse
functions.description: Comparator function to order documents by their tab order in reverse (right-to-left). Suitable for use with GLib sorting APIs; returns negative/zero/positive as a is less than/equal to/greater than b.
requirements: a and b must point to GeanyDocument* (or pointers to such) as expected by the caller’s container/iteration context.

functions.name: document_find_by_id
functions.description: Finds an open document by its pseudo-unique ID (GeanyDocument::id). Returns the matching document or NULL if not found.
requirements: id must be a non-zero value (0 is reserved as an unused value).

functions.name: editor_get_type
functions.description: Returns the GObject type identifier for the Geany editor class. Typically used for type registration/introspection within GTK/GObject code.
requirements: No arguments required.
Return value is a GType and can be compared/used with GObject/GTK APIs.
May be called at any time after the library is loaded.

functions.name: editor_get_indent_prefs
functions.description: Retrieves the effective indentation preferences for the given editor/document, including project or filetype overrides when applicable. Use this to determine width, type (tabs/spaces/both), auto-indent mode, and related settings.
requirements: editor must be a valid, initialized GeanyEditor pointer.
The returned pointer is owned by the editor; do not modify or free it.
Behavior is undefined if editor is NULL.

functions.name: editor_create_widget
functions.description: Creates and returns the Scintilla editor widget associated with the given GeanyEditor. Use this to obtain the underlying ScintillaObject for embedding or further configuration.
requirements: editor must be a valid, initialized GeanyEditor pointer.
Return value is a ScintillaObject (a GtkWidget subtype); ownership/ lifetime are managed by Geany/editor (do not unref/free unless the API explicitly specifies).
Behavior is undefined if editor is NULL.

functions.name: editor_indicator_set_on_range
functions.signature: void editor_indicator_set_on_range(GeanyEditor *editor, gint indic, gint start, gint end);
functions.description: Enables an indicator (e.g., error underline, search highlight) on a specified character range within the document.
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.
indic must be a valid indicator index (e.g., values from GeanyIndicator or a Scintilla indicator number).
start and end are document character positions; they should be within the current document bounds and typically 0-based.
start should be less than or equal to end.
No return value; caller should ensure positions are valid to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: editor_indicator_set_on_line
functions.signature: void editor_indicator_set_on_line(GeanyEditor *editor, gint indic, gint line);
functions.description: Enables an indicator on the specified line, highlighting that line according to the indicator style.
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.
indic must be a valid indicator index (e.g., a GeanyIndicator value).
line is a 0-based line index and should refer to an existing line in the document.
No return value; caller should ensure the line is within range.

functions.name: editor_indicator_clear
functions.description: Clears all uses of a specific indicator throughout the document, removing any highlights previously set with that indicator.
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.
indic must be a valid indicator index used in this editor.
No return value.

functions.name: editor_set_indent_type
functions.description: Sets the indentation type (spaces, tabs, or both) for the given editor instance.
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.
type must be one of the GeanyIndentType enum values: GEANY_INDENT_TYPE_SPACES, GEANY_INDENT_TYPE_TABS, or GEANY_INDENT_TYPE_BOTH.

functions.name: editor_set_indent_width
functions.description: Sets the indentation width for the editor (number of spaces per indent unit; behavior with tabs depends on indent type).
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.
width should be a positive integer (> 0).
For GEANY_INDENT_TYPE_BOTH, this interacts with hard_tab_width; exact behavior is determined by editor prefs.

functions.name: editor_get_word_at_pos
functions.description: Returns the word at the specified character position, using the provided set of characters considered part of a word. Useful for symbol lookup, autocompletion, or selection logic.
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.
pos should be a valid 0-based character position within the document.
wordchars should point to a NUL-terminated string of characters treated as word constituents (e.g., GEANY_WORDCHARS).
The returned gchar* is heap-allocated and must be freed by the caller with g_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: editor_get_eol_char_name
functions.description: Gets the human-readable name of the current end-of-line mode for the editor (e.g., LF, CRLF, or CR).
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.
The returned string is owned by the editor or static storage; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: editor_get_eol_char_len
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of the end-of-line sequence used by the editor (typically 1 for LF/CR or 2 for CRLF).
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.

functions.name: editor_get_eol_char
functions.description: Returns the end-of-line character sequence used by the editor (e.g., "\n", "\r\n", or "\r").
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.
The returned pointer refers to a constant buffer; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: editor_insert_text_block
functions.signature: void editor_insert_text_block(GeanyEditor *editor, const gchar *text, gint insert_pos, gint cursor_index, gint newline_indent_size, gboolean replace_newlines);
functions.description: Inserts a block of text into the document at the specified position, optionally adjusting indentation for newlines and controlling how newline characters are handled. The caret can be positioned relative to the inserted text via cursor_index.
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.
text must be a valid NUL-terminated UTF-8 string.
insert_pos should be a valid 0-based character position within the document at which to insert.
cursor_index should refer to a character index within the provided text (or a sentinel value if supported by implementation; exact special values are unknown).
newline_indent_size should be a non-negative integer.
If replace_newlines is TRUE, newline handling within text may be normalized to the editor's EOL mode (exact behavior not documented here).

functions.name: editor_get_eol_char_mode
functions.description: Returns the current end-of-line mode as an integer enum value understood by the editor/Scintilla (e.g., LF/CRLF/CR).
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.
Return value is an implementation-defined integer corresponding to the EOL mode.

functions.name: editor_goto_pos
functions.signature: gboolean editor_goto_pos(GeanyEditor *editor, gint pos, gboolean mark);
functions.description: Moves the caret to the specified document position. When mark is TRUE, the previous caret position is used to create or extend a selection (i.e., mark the range). Returns TRUE on success.
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.
pos should be a valid 0-based character position within the document.
mark controls whether a selection is created/extended from the previous caret position.

functions.name: editor_find_snippet
functions.description: Finds a snippet by name in the editor's snippet registry and returns its template/string if available, or NULL if not found.
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.
snippet_name must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string naming the snippet to find.
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is owned by the editor/snippet system; do not modify or free it.

functions.name: editor_insert_snippet
functions.signature: void editor_insert_snippet(GeanyEditor *editor, gint pos, const gchar *snippet);
functions.description: Inserts the given snippet text at the specified position, expanding any snippet syntax supported by Geany. Useful for programmatically inserting templates.
requirements: editor must be a valid GeanyEditor pointer.
pos should be a valid 0-based character position within the document.
snippet must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string containing the snippet to insert.

functions.name: encodings_convert_to_utf8
functions.description: Converts the given byte buffer from an unknown/source encoding to UTF-8. It likely attempts known encodings and, on success, returns a UTF-8 encoded string. If used_encoding is non-NULL, it will be set to the name of the encoding that was detected/used. Typical GLib/Geany patterns suggest the returned string should be freed with g_free, and NULL may be returned on failure. Exact detection strategy and ownership of used_encoding are not documented in this header and are therefore partially unknown.
requirements: buffer must point to readable memory containing the input bytes; its lifetime must outlive the call.
size specifies the number of bytes to read from buffer; if negative-size behavior (e.g., -1 meaning NUL-terminated) is supported is unknown from this header.

If used_encoding is not NULL, it must be a valid pointer to receive an encoding name; whether the assigned string must be freed by the caller is not specified here (likely g_free per GLib conventions).
Callers should handle a NULL return value as a conversion/detection failure and avoid dereferencing it.
Input data should be valid in at least one of the supported encodings; otherwise conversion may fail.

functions.name: encodings_convert_to_utf8_from_charset
functions.signature: gchar *encodings_convert_to_utf8_from_charset(const gchar *buffer, gssize size, const gchar *charset, gboolean fast);
functions.description: Converts the given byte buffer from the specified charset to UTF-8. When fast is TRUE, the function performs no additional checks beyond the direct conversion attempt (per the comment), which may be faster but less robust. Returns a UTF-8 string on success, otherwise likely NULL. The returned string is typically newly allocated and should be freed with g_free (inferred from GLib conventions).
requirements: buffer must point to readable memory containing the input bytes for at least size bytes.
size is the number of bytes to convert; whether negative values have special meaning is not specified here.
charset must name a supported encoding; passing an unsupported or NULL charset may cause conversion to fail (behavior not fully specified).
When fast is TRUE, callers should not expect validation or heuristic checks; invalid sequences may cause failure or undefined conversion results depending on implementation.
Callers should check for a NULL return and handle conversion errors appropriately before using the result.
The returned UTF-8 string likely requires the caller to free it with g_free (inferred).

functions.name: encodings_get_charset_from_index
functions.description: Returns the charset name string corresponding to the given encoding index (likely a value from GeanyEncodingIndex). Useful to map an index to its canonical charset identifier. The returned pointer is const; it likely refers to static storage and must not be modified or freed.
requirements: idx should be a valid encoding index, typically within the range [0, GEANY_ENCODINGS_MAX-1] (inferred from the enum).
Callers must not modify or free the returned const gchar*; treat it as read-only and potentially static.
If idx is out of range, the function may return NULL (behavior not documented here; callers should check for NULL).

functions.name: filetypes_detect_from_file
functions.description: Detects and returns the GeanyFiletype corresponding to a given filename. Intended to guess the filetype from the UTF-8-encoded path (typically by extension and/or patterns). Returns a pointer to the detected filetype or possibly NULL/“None” if unknown (behavior not documented here).
requirements: utf8_filename: should be a UTF-8 encoded filename/path (inferred from parameter name).
utf8_filename: should reference an existing or plausible filename string; NULL handling and behavior for non-existent files are not documented.
Return value may be NULL or a special “None” filetype if detection fails; callers should be prepared to handle non-detections (exact contract unknown).

functions.name: filetypes_lookup_by_name
functions.description: Looks up a filetype by its internal, untranslated short name (e.g., "C", "None"). Useful for retrieving a GeanyFiletype when you know the canonical name used for lookups.
requirements: name: must match the untranslated short name used internally (as noted in the GeanyFiletype::name comment).
name: should be a valid, null-terminated UTF-8 string; NULL handling is not documented.
Caller must handle the case where no matching filetype exists (return value unspecified here, likely NULL).

functions.name: filetypes_index
functions.description: Returns the GeanyFiletype at the given index from Geany’s filetypes array. Serves as an accessor equivalent to using the filetypes array directly.
requirements: idx: should refer to a valid index within the filetypes array (typically 0..filetypes_array->len-1); behavior for out-of-range indices is not documented.
Caller should not assume the returned pointer is non-NULL for invalid indices; handle potential NULL safely (behavior unknown).
The returned GeanyFiletype is owned by Geany; do not free or modify memory ownership semantics.

functions.name: filetypes_get_display_name
functions.description: Returns the user-visible, display name for the given filetype (as opposed to the untranslated internal short name). Intended for UI presentation and localization.
requirements: ft: should be a valid, initialized GeanyFiletype pointer; NULL handling is not documented.
The returned string is owned by Geany; treat it as read-only and do not free it.

functions.name: filetypes_get_sorted_by_name
functions.description: Returns a read-only singly-linked list of filetypes sorted by name (likely display name). Useful for iterating over filetypes in a stable, name-sorted order.
requirements: The returned GSList and its elements are owned by Geany; do not modify or free them.
List element type is inferred to be GeanyFiletype*; callers should cast accordingly.
Sorting key (internal vs. display name) is not explicitly documented; do not rely on a specific collation beyond general name sorting.

functions.name: filetype_get_type
functions.description: Returns the GType for the GeanyFiletype type. Standard GLib/GObject type getter used for runtime type information and bindings.
requirements: May be called at any time after the library is loaded; no arguments required.
Return value is a valid GType identifier; no ownership transfer.

functions.name: highlighting_get_style
functions.description: Looks up the lexer style attributes (colors and font flags) for a given filetype and style ID. Intended for querying the configured Scintilla style parameters that Geany applies for a filetype. Returns a pointer to a const GeanyLexerStyle describing foreground/background colors (0xBBGGRR), bold, and italic. The availability of a style depends on Geany’s style tables for the filetype; details on invalid IDs are not documented here.
requirements: ft_id must refer to a valid Geany filetype identifier.
style_id must be a valid style index/ID for the lexer used by the filetype.
Callers must not modify the returned GeanyLexerStyle (it is const).
The returned pointer may be NULL or invalid if the IDs are not recognized (behavior not documented here); callers should handle a NULL result safely.

functions.name: highlighting_set_styles
functions.description: Applies the configured syntax highlighting styles to a Scintilla widget for the specified Geany filetype. Typical usage is to call this after setting the Scintilla lexer for a document or when the color scheme/filetype changes.
requirements: sci must point to a valid, initialized ScintillaObject (Scintilla widget).
ft must point to a valid, initialized GeanyFiletype describing the intended lexer/filetype.
The Scintilla instance should have an appropriate lexer set that matches the filetype, or styles may not align with style IDs.
Function performs in-place configuration of styles on the widget; no return value, callers should not expect error reporting except via external logging.

functions.name: highlighting_is_string_style
functions.description: Determines whether the given style ID for the specified lexer corresponds to a string literal style. Useful to check if a Scintilla position/style represents string content.
requirements: lexer must be a valid Scintilla lexer identifier for which Geany has style mappings.
style must be a valid style ID for the given lexer.
Return value is TRUE if the style is considered a string style, otherwise FALSE.

functions.name: highlighting_is_comment_style
functions.description: Determines whether the given style ID for the specified lexer corresponds to a comment style. Useful for logic that treats comments specially (e.g., spellcheck, folding, or ignoring code actions).
requirements: lexer must be a valid Scintilla lexer identifier for which Geany has style mappings.
style must be a valid style ID for the given lexer.
Return value is TRUE if the style is considered a comment style, otherwise FALSE.

functions.name: highlighting_is_code_style
functions.description: Determines whether the given style ID for the specified lexer is considered code (as opposed to comments, strings, etc.). Can be used to restrict operations to actual code regions.
requirements: lexer must be a valid Scintilla lexer identifier for which Geany has style mappings.
style must be a valid style ID for the given lexer.
Return value is TRUE if the style is considered a code style, otherwise FALSE.

functions.name: keybindings_send_command
functions.description: Dispatches/executes the keybinding action identified by key_id within the keybinding group identified by group_id. Intended for programmatically triggering the same behavior as if the user pressed the bound key combination.
requirements: group_id must refer to a valid keybinding group (e.g., a value from GeanyKeyGroupID).
key_id must refer to a valid command within the specified group (e.g., a value from GeanyKeyBindingID when applicable).
Behavior when IDs do not match an existing binding is unknown (not documented).

functions.name: keybindings_set_item
functions.signature: GeanyKeyBinding *keybindings_set_item(GeanyKeyGroup *group, gsize key_id, GeanyKeyCallback callback, guint key, GdkModifierType mod, const gchar *name, const gchar *label, GtkWidget *menu_item);
functions.description: Registers/updates a single keybinding in the given group. Associates an optional callback (without userdata), a default key and modifier, a configuration name, a human-readable label, and optionally links the binding to a menu item so its accelerator is updated.
requirements: group must be a valid, initialized GeanyKeyGroup pointer.
key_id must designate a valid index/slot within the group (exact range limits are not documented).
callback may be NULL to use the group callback instead (as noted in GeanyKeyBinding docs).
key is a GDK key value (e.g., GDK_KEY_a) or 0 for unassigned.
mod is a GdkModifierType bitmask or 0 for no modifiers; use keybindings_get_modifiers() when testing for the primary modifier.
name must be a non-NULL configuration key string (used in keyfile).
label should be a user-visible description; underscores may be included (they won’t be displayed).
menu_item may be NULL or a valid GtkWidget to attach the accelerator to.
Return value is a GeanyKeyBinding pointer; NULL return conditions are unknown (not documented).

functions.name: keybindings_set_item_full
functions.signature: GeanyKeyBinding *keybindings_set_item_full(GeanyKeyGroup *group, gsize key_id, guint key, GdkModifierType mod, const gchar *kf_name, const gchar *label, GtkWidget *menu_item, GeanyKeyBindingFunc func, gpointer pdata, GDestroyNotify destroy_notify);
functions.description: Registers/updates a keybinding like keybindings_set_item(), but uses a callback that receives the GeanyKeyBinding, the key ID, and a userdata pointer, along with an optional destroy notifier for that userdata. Provides more flexible callbacks with context.
requirements: group must be a valid, initialized GeanyKeyGroup pointer.
key_id must designate a valid index/slot within the group (exact range limits are not documented).
key is a GDK key value or 0 for unassigned.
mod is a GdkModifierType bitmask or 0; use keybindings_get_modifiers() when testing for primary modifier keys.
kf_name must be a non-NULL configuration key string (stored in the keyfile).
label should be a user-visible description; underscores may be included (they won’t be displayed).
menu_item may be NULL or a valid GtkWidget to attach the accelerator to.
func may be NULL to defer to the group callback (per GeanyKeyBinding documentation).
pdata is an optional userdata pointer passed to func; its lifetime can be managed via destroy_notify.
destroy_notify may be NULL or a valid GDestroyNotify to clean up pdata when the binding is freed.
Return value is a GeanyKeyBinding pointer; NULL return conditions are unknown (not documented).

functions.name: keybindings_get_item
functions.description: Retrieves the GeanyKeyBinding structure for the given key_id within the specified group.
requirements: group must be a valid GeanyKeyGroup pointer.
key_id must refer to an existing item within the group (exact bounds are not documented).
Returns a pointer to the binding; behavior for out-of-range or missing items (e.g., returning NULL) is unknown (not documented).

functions.name: keybindings_get_modifiers
functions.description: Normalizes a modifier mask for keybinding checks by adding the platform-specific primary modifier (GEANY_PRIMARY_MOD_MASK) when appropriate. Use this when testing for modifier presence to be portable across platforms.
requirements: mods should be a GdkModifierType bitmask composed of valid GDK modifier flags.
Function returns a GdkModifierType mask; no error reporting is documented.

functions.name: keybindings_load_keyfile
functions.description: Loads keybinding definitions from the configuration keyfile into the application’s keybinding system.
requirements: Must be called in a context where the keybinding system and configuration paths are initialized (exact ordering relative to initialization is not documented).
No return value; error handling behavior is not documented.

functions.name: main_reload_configuration
functions.description: Reloads Geany’s configuration at runtime. Intended to re-read user or system settings and apply them without restarting the application. Typical usage is after configuration files change to refresh in-memory settings.
requirements: Must be called when the Geany core is initialized; exact initialization preconditions are unknown (not documented).
Thread-safety and calling context (e.g., main/UI thread) are unknown; callers should assume default application thread usage unless otherwise documented.

functions.description: Initializes Geany’s localization/i18n. Sets up the gettext domain and locale data so UI strings are translated using the specified gettext package and locale directory.

Thread-safety and whether it may be called more than once are unknown.

functions.name: main_is_realized
functions.description: Returns whether Geany’s main window has been realized (created and mapped by the GUI framework). Useful to check UI readiness before performing operations requiring a realized main window.
requirements: No parameters.
May be called at any time; meaning is only relevant after application initialization (inferred).
Return value is a GLib gboolean (TRUE/FALSE).

functions.name: geany_is_closing_all_documents
functions.description: Indicates whether Geany is currently in the process of closing all open documents as a batch operation. Can be used by callers to suppress actions or signals that should not trigger during mass-close.
requirements: No parameters.
Return value is a GLib gboolean (TRUE/FALSE).
The exact lifetime and thread-safety of this state flag are unknown; intended for use during document/tabs management (inferred from name and related comments).

functions.name: msgwin_status_add
functions.description: Appends a formatted status message to the status tab of Geany’s message window. Usage mirrors printf-style formatting: pass a format string followed by the corresponding arguments.
requirements: format must be a valid non-NULL printf-style format string.
The variadic arguments must match the provided format string in number and type (printf-compatible).
Strings passed should be valid UTF-8 as per GLib conventions.

functions.name: msgwin_status_add_string

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces UTF-8 bytes representing a plausible filesystem path or filename.
# It targets fuzz stubs that call FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() and FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for paths and
# short names. We generate a short, valid, ASCII path that likely exists in common environments
# to exercise both success and failure paths:
# - Absolute paths under /tmp, /var/tmp, /home/<user>, /etc, current dir relative names
# - Include directories and a leaf filename with common extensions
# - Occasionally produce a directory path (ending with '/') to test directory-oriented APIs
# - Avoid NULs and exotic characters; keep <= 255 bytes total and <= 4096 requirement

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."
EXTS = [
    "c", "h", "cpp", "hpp", "py", "txt", "md", "json", "xml", "ini", "conf",
    "sh", "Makefile", "log", "yaml", "toml", "cs", "java", "rb", "go", "rs"
]
DIR_COMPONENTS = [
    "src", "include", "lib", "build", "bin", "obj", "docs", "config", "test",
    "tests", "examples", "data", "tmp", "var", "cache"
]

def _rand_component(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure component doesn't start with a dot unless explicitly chosen
    comp = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n)).strip()
    comp = comp.replace(" ", "_")
    if not comp:
        comp = "x"
    # Avoid reserved names seen on Windows even if not used: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1, LPT1
    reserved = {"CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL"} | {f"COM{i}" for i in range(1,10)} | {f"LPT{i}" for i in range(1,10)}
    if comp.upper() in reserved:
        comp = comp + "_"
    return comp

def _rand_leaf(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Sometimes return an extension-like file, sometimes a special name like Makefile
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        return "Makefile"
    name = _rand_component(rng, 3, 16)
    # Occasionally create multi-dot names
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        mid = _rand_component(rng, 2, 6)
        name = f"{name}.{mid}"
    ext = rng.choice(EXTS)
    # Some entries in EXTS are full names (e.g., Makefile). Guard against double dots
    if ext == "Makefile":
        return ext
    return f"{name}.{ext}"

def _candidate_roots() -> List[str]:
    roots = []
    # Common Unix roots
    roots.extend(["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/etc", "/usr", "/opt", "/home"])  # may not exist but plausible
    # Current working directory and a relative start
    roots.append(os.getcwd() or ".")
    roots.append(".")
    # If HOME is set, include it
    home = os.environ.get("HOME")
    if home:
        roots.append(home)
    # Windows-like drive root if on Windows
    if os.name == "nt":
        roots.append(os.path.splitdrive(os.getcwd())[0] + os.sep if os.getcwd() else "C:\\")
    return list(dict.fromkeys(roots))

def _build_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    root = rng.choice(_candidate_roots())
    sep = os.sep
    # Normalize root without trailing separator (except for drive root)
    if len(root) > 1:
        root = root.rstrip("/\\")
    depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
    comps = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        comps.append(rng.choice(DIR_COMPONENTS) if rng.random() < 0.5 else _rand_component(rng))
    # Choose to end as directory vs file
    as_dir = rng.random() < 0.25
    if as_dir and not comps:
        comps.append(_rand_component(rng))
    leaf = None if as_dir else _rand_leaf(rng)
    parts = [p for p in ([root] + comps + ([leaf] if leaf else [])) if p]
    path = sep.join(parts)
    # Occasionally ensure directory suffix with separator
    if as_dir and not path.endswith(sep):
        path = path + sep
    # Length guard
    if len(path) > 255:
        path = path[:255].rstrip("/\\")
    return path or "."

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Produce multiple candidates and pick one with a mix of existing/non-existing likelihoods
    path = _build_path(rng)
    # Small chance to force a very simple basename
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        path = _rand_leaf(rng)
    # Small chance to produce just a directory marker like "." or ".."
    if rng.random() < 0.05:
        path = rng.choice([".", "..", os.sep])
    # Ensure ASCII, strip any accidental disallowed characters
    path_ascii = ''.join(ch for ch in path if ch in SAFE_CHARS or ch in "/\\:")
    if not path_ascii:
        path_ascii = "."
    # Bound total size
    path_ascii = path_ascii[:1024]
    return path_ascii.encode("utf-8")

# Data type: filename/identifier string
# Used by stubs:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(): expects a valid filename path string
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): used as short name/identifier; should be non-empty and avoid path separators
# Also integers consumed internally come from a separate FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int), so our buffer
# only needs to provide bytes for strings/files that the harness maps to FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME/STR.
#
# Goals:
# - Provide realistic file paths with extensions and nested directories so basename extraction works.
# - Provide filenames that exercise utils_remove_ext_from_filename (multiple dots, hidden files, no ext).
# - Provide varied filetype-relevant extensions to hit templates_get_template_fileheader for many types.
# - Provide short identifier strings without slashes, including Unicode and edge cases.
#
# Buffer format (simple, self-describing, newline-separated records):
#   PATHS:\n
#   <path1>\n
#   <path2>\n
#   ...\n
#   ---\n
#   NAMES:\n
#   <name1>\n
#   <name2>\n
#   ...\n# The fuzzer harness typically pulls strings sequentially; providing many candidates increases coverage.
# Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

COMMON_EXTS = [
    # Map to Geany filetypes when possible
    "c", "h", "cpp", "hpp", "cc", "hh",
    "java", "py", "rb", "lua", "js", "ts", "css", "html", "xml", "yml", "yaml",
    "json", "toml", "ini", "conf", "md", "rst", "tex",
    "go", "rs", "zig", "nim", "vala", "cs", "php", "pl", "pm", "sh", "bash",
    "sql", "make", "cmake", "glsl", "asm", "s", "f", "f90", "vhdl", "sv",
    "po", "diff", "patch", "coffee", "gd", "r", "jl", "dart", "nix",
]

MULTI_DOT_CANDIDATES = [
    "archive.tar.gz",
    "module.min.js",
    "Makefile.am",
    "config.site.local",
]

HIDDEN_CANDIDATES = [
    ".gitignore", ".editorconfig", ".clang-format", ".env", ".bashrc"
]

DIR_NAMES = [
    "src", "include", "lib", "build", "tests", "examples", "doc", "scripts",
    "third_party", "vendor", "assets", "data"
]

# Some unicode-friendly names (no slashes)
UNICODE_NAMES = [
    "naïve", "résumé", "über", "café", "smörgåsbord", "Δelta", "πroject", "東京", "文件", "файл",
]

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"


def rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=24) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure starts with alnum to be nicer as identifier
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits)
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return first + rest


def rand_ext(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.85:
        return rng.choice(COMMON_EXTS)
    # rare random extension
    return rand_ident(rng, 1, 4).lower()


def rand_basename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.2:
        return rng.choice(HIDDEN_CANDIDATES)
    if choice < 0.35:
        return rng.choice(MULTI_DOT_CANDIDATES)
    if choice < 0.5:
        # no extension
        return rand_ident(rng)
    # with extension
    name = rand_ident(rng)
    ext = rand_ext(rng)
    return f"{name}.{ext}"


def rand_dir_path(rng: random.Random, depth_range=(0, 3)) -> str:
    depth = rng.randint(*depth_range)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            parts.append(rand_ident(rng))
        else:
            parts.append(rng.choice(DIR_NAMES))
    # join with forward slash to match stub's basename logic
    return "/".join(parts)


def make_paths(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> List[str]:
    paths: List[str] = []
    # Seed with some absolute and relative
    base_counts = rng.randint(12, 24)
    for _ in range(base_counts):
        dirpath = rand_dir_path(rng)
        base = rand_basename(rng)
        if dirpath:
            path = f"/{dirpath}/{base}" if rng.random() < 0.7 else f"{dirpath}/{base}"
        else:
            path = base if rng.random() < 0.5 else f"./{base}"
        # Normalize accidental double slashes (unlikely)
        path = path.replace("//", "/")
        paths.append(path)
    # Add some Windows-like paths (even if not used, basenames still work on slash parsing)
    drive = chr(rng.randint(ord('C'), ord('H')))
    win_parts = [rng.choice(DIR_NAMES), rng.choice(DIR_NAMES), rand_ident(rng)]
    win_base = rand_basename(rng)
    win_path = drive + ":\\" + "\\".join(win_parts + [win_base])
    # Convert to forward slashes to still be a valid path per stub usage, but include backslashes sample too
    paths.append(win_path)
    paths.append(win_path.replace("\\", "/"))
    # Add a long multi-dot file
    long_multi = ".".join([rand_ident(rng, 3, 6) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6))])
    paths.append(long_multi)
    # Ensure some template-targeting extensions explicitly
    for ext in ["c", "cpp", "py", "java", "xml", "toml", "zig", "rs", "go", "md"]:
        paths.append(f"/project/{ext}/main.{ext}")
    return paths


def make_names(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> List[str]:
    names: List[str] = []
    # Guaranteed non-empty simple names
    for _ in range(count // 2):
        names.append(rand_ident(rng))
    # Unicode and edge-y but valid identifiers (no slashes)
    names.extend(UNICODE_NAMES[: rng.randint(3, len(UNICODE_NAMES))])
    # Names with dots (to test short name not being a path)
    for _ in range(max(3, count // 4)):
        names.append(rand_ident(rng) + "." + rand_ext(rng))
    # Very short
    names.append("_")
    names.append("a")
    # Long but within reasonable UI length
    names.append(rand_ident(rng, 24, 48))
    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for n in names:
        if n not in seen:
            seen.add(n)
            out.append(n)
    return out


def assemble(paths: List[str], names: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Compose as sections
    parts: List[str] = []
    parts.append("PATHS:")
    parts.extend(paths)
    parts.append("---")
    parts.append("NAMES:")
    parts.extend(names)
    blob = "\n".join(parts) + "\n"
    data = blob.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        # Trim lists to fit budget
        # Reserve ~128 bytes for headers and some names
        budget = MAX_SIZE - 128
        half = budget // 2
        p_blob = ("\n".join(["PATHS:"] + paths) + "\n").encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        if len(p_blob) > half:
            # shrink paths
            keep = max(4, int(len(paths) * half / len(p_blob)))
            p_blob = ("\n".join(["PATHS:"] + paths[:keep]) + "\n").encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        n_blob = ("\n".join(["NAMES:"] + names) + "\n").encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        if len(n_blob) > half:
            keepn = max(4, int(len(names) * half / len(n_blob)))
            n_blob = ("\n".join(["NAMES:"] + names[:keepn]) + "\n").encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        data = p_blob + b"---\n" + n_blob
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Create a diverse pool while respecting size limit
    paths = make_paths(rng, MAX_SIZE // 2)
    names = make_names(rng, rng.randint(12, 28))
    return assemble(paths, names)

import random

# Data type: identifier string
# Goal: produce short ASCII/UTF-8 identifiers suitable for:
#  - snippet names (editor_find_snippet)
#  - filetype lookup short names (filetypes_lookup_by_name)
#  - keybinding names/labels and keyfile names (keybindings_set_item/_full)
#  - plugin extension names (plugin_extension_register)
#  - stash key names (stash_group_* add functions)
# Characteristics:
#  - Prefer [A-Za-z0-9_-.] and simple ASCII words
#  - Vary case, separators, and include known candidates to trigger lookups
#  - Keep length modest (<= 64)
#  - No newlines or NULs
#  - Sometimes return known values like "C", "CPP", "Python", etc.

KNOWN_FILETYPES = [
    "C", "CPP", "Python", "None", "Make", "Lua", "Markdown",
    "JavaScript", "HTML", "XML"
]

# Common snippet-like names
KNOWN_SNIPPETS = [
    "for", "if", "while", "func", "class", "main", "printf",
    "include_guard", "hdr", "test", "todo", "trycatch",
]

# Reasonable words for labels/names
WORDS = [
    "open", "save", "compile", "build", "run", "search", "replace",
    "goto", "toggle", "wrap", "indent", "unindent", "zoom", "fold",
    "unfold", "marker", "snippet", "autocomplete", "calltip", "status",
    "messages", "project", "tools", "editor", "document", "sidebar",
]

SEPARATORS = ["_", "-", "."]

def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    # Identifier with alnum and _.-, starting with letter for safety
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters)
    rest_len = rng.randint(max(0, min_len-1), max_len-1)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_.-"
    rest = "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(rest_len))
    return first + rest

def _join_words(rng: random.Random, words: List[str]) -> str:
    parts = rng.sample(words, rng.randint(1, min(3, len(words))))
    sep = rng.choice(SEPARATORS)
    s = sep.join(parts)
    # Optionally add numeric suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        s += sep + str(rng.randint(1, 999))
    return s

def _maybe_case(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    mode = rng.randint(0, 3)
    if mode == 0:
        return s.lower()
    if mode == 1:
        return s.upper()
    if mode == 2:
        # title/camel-ish
        return "".join(part.capitalize() for part in s.replace('-', '_').replace('.', '_').split('_'))
    return s

def _pick_known(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    pool = KNOWN_FILETYPES + KNOWN_SNIPPETS
    return rng.choice(pool)

def _generate_identifier(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Weighted strategies to cover different consumers
    p = rng.random()
    if p < 0.20:
        # Exact known filetype/snippet to hit lookup paths
        s = _pick_known(rng)
    elif p < 0.45:
        # Combined words with separator
        s = _join_words(rng, WORDS)
    elif p < 0.70:
        # Simple identifier
        s = _rand_ident(rng, 1, rng.randint(6, 24))
    else:
        # Mix known head with suffix/prefix
        base = _pick_known(rng)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s = base + rng.choice(SEPARATORS) + _rand_ident(rng, 1, 8)
        else:
            s = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 6) + rng.choice(SEPARATORS) + base
    s = _maybe_case(rng, s)
    # Enforce maximum length constraints used by stubs (<= 64)
    if len(s) > 64:
        s = s[:64]
    # Ensure non-empty and ASCII-safe
    if not s:
        s = "x"
    return s

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    s = _generate_identifier(rng)
    # Return as bytes (UTF-8)
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    # Ensure size limits
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: "character class set" used by editor_get_word_at_pos as wordchars.
# The fuzzer stub also uses FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) for a position and FUZZ_PARAM_STR for wordchars.
# We will craft a seedable generator that emits a compact buffer containing:
# - A 32-bit unsigned integer (little-endian) used as the random position source.
# - One or more NUL-terminated strings that the harness will draw from via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
#   The first string should be an interesting word-character set; we may append additional
#   strings to increase variety for other consumers. The harness typically consumes strings
#   sequentially from the provided buffer.
#
# Design:
# - Position value: choose a variety of numbers that will exercise start, middle, and end positions
#   when modulo doc_len is applied (e.g., large primes, 0, near-INT_MAX patterns).
# - Wordchar sets: provide multiple curated sets to trigger different behaviors:
#   * ASCII alnum + underscore (typical identifier)
#   * Letters only
#   * Digits only
#   * Underscore only
#   * Unicode-like extended sets approximated with ASCII fallbacks (since consumers often expect UTF-8)
#   * Punctuation-heavy set to reduce matches
#   * Empty string (but stub replaces empty with default; still interesting for path)
#   * Mixed sets including dash and dot to allow file-like tokens
# - Ensure each string is <= 128 bytes as the stub truncates beyond that.
# - Terminate each string with NUL. Limit total buffer <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_BUF = 4096

# Curated word-char sets (<=128 bytes each)
CURATED_SETS: List[str] = [
    "_ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789",
    "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz",
    "0123456789",
    "_",
    # Mix including dash and dot (common in CSS/hosts-like names)
    "-._ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789",
    # Hex-only
    "ABCDEFabcdef0123456789",
    # Camel-case friendly (letters + digits, no underscore)
    "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789",
    # Minimal letters to isolate short words
    "aeiouAEIOU",
    # Punctuation heavy to collapse most words
    "-._",
    # Empty set: will trigger fallback in the stub
    "",
]

# Additional generator for random custom sets staying within printable ASCII
def random_set(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    # Choose from a broad but safe printable set
    base = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-."  # common token constituents
    # Occasionally add other punctuation to shrink matches
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base += ":@#$"  # still safe printable
    k = rng.randint(0, max_len)  # allow empty as well
    # Use set() to avoid duplicates, but preserve order by sampling without replacement
    # However, random.sample requires k<=len(base); cap accordingly
    k = min(k, len(base))
    chars = rng.sample(base, k)
    return "".join(chars)

# Interesting 32-bit numbers for positions
INTERESTING_UINT32 = [
    0,
    1,
    2,
    7,
    15,
    31,
    63,
    127,
    255,
    256,
    511,
    1023,
    4095,
    0x7FFFFFFF,
    0x80000000,
    0xFFFFFFFF,
    123456789,
    314159265,
    271828182,
]


def _u32_le(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((n & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF, (n >> 16) & 0xFF, (n >> 24) & 0xFF))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build buffer incrementally
    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Position source: pick from interesting values or random
    if rng.random() < 0.75:
        pos = rng.choice(INTERESTING_UINT32)
    else:
        pos = rng.getrandbits(32)
    chunks.append(_u32_le(pos))

    # 2) Provide a sequence of NUL-terminated strings for FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumption.
    # Ensure at least one high-quality wordchar set first.
    # Choose 1 from curated sets, 1 random set, and then some extras.
    strings: List[str] = []

    # Primary curated set
    strings.append(rng.choice(CURATED_SETS))

    # One random custom set
    strings.append(random_set(rng))

    # Add a few additional curated/random entries to diversify consumption across stubs
    extra_count = rng.randint(2, 6)
    for _ in range(extra_count):
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            s = rng.choice(CURATED_SETS)
        else:
            s = random_set(rng)
        strings.append(s)

    # Encode as NUL-terminated UTF-8 strings, truncating to 128 bytes as per stub cap
    total = len(b"".join(chunks))
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8')[:128]
        # Ensure not empty too often; occasionally force empty to trigger fallback
        if len(b) == 0 and rng.random() < 0.7:
            b = b"_ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
        seg = b + b"\x00"
        if total + len(seg) > MAX_BUF:
            break
        chunks.append(seg)
        total += len(seg)

    # If buffer is too small (e.g., only pos and one string), pad with another safe set
    if total < 16:
        pad = b"_ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789\x00"
        if total + len(pad) <= MAX_BUF:
            chunks.append(pad)

    return b"".join(chunks)

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# We generate arbitrary byte buffers that are likely valid text in a variety of
# encodings commonly recognized by iconv/glib, to improve chances that
# encodings_convert_to_utf8 and encodings_convert_to_utf8_from_charset succeed.
# We mix UTF-8, UTF-16LE/BE with and without BOM, UTF-32LE/BE, ISO-8859-* text,
# Windows-1252, Shift_JIS, EUC-JP, GBK/GB18030, Big5, and also XML-like
# snippets to exercise utils_find_open_xml_tag(_pos).

MAX_LEN = 4096

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"Hello", b"world", b"Geany", b"Scintilla", b"plugin", b"encoding",
    b"UTF-8", b"ISO-8859-1", b"Windows-1252", b"regex", b"snippet",
    b"function", b"variable", b"namespace", b"class", b"struct", b"enum",
]
XML_SNIPPETS = [
    b"<root><child attr=\"v\">text</child></root>",
    b"<note><to>Tove</to><from>Jani</from>",  # intentionally unclosed root
    b"<a><b><c></c>",  # open tags left
    b"<tag xmlns=\"urn:x\"><inner/></tag>",
    b"<!-- comment --><x>y</x>",
]

# Some byte sequences representative of various legacy encodings.
# These are approximate and not exhaustive; aim is to be valid often.
WIN1252_BYTES = bytes([
    0x48,0x65,0x6C,0x6C,0x6F,0x20, # Hello 
    0x93, 0x57, 0x6F, 0x72, 0x6C, 0x64, 0x94, # “World” smart quotes
    0x20, 0xA3, 0x20, 0x80, # £ and Euro
])
ISO_8859_1_BYTES = b"Cafe \xe9lan r\xe9sum\xe9 a\xe7ai\xef\xbb\xbf"[:30]
# Some CJK in various encodings (likely decodable by common iconv tables)
SHIFT_JIS_BYTES = bytes([0x82, 0xA0, 0x82, 0xA2, 0x82, 0xA4, 0x81, 0x40, 0x83, 0x65, 0x83, 0x58])
EUC_JP_BYTES = bytes([0xA4,0xA2,0xA4,0xA4,0xA4,0xA6,0xA1,0xA1])
GBK_BYTES = bytes([0xC4,0xE3,0xBA,0xC3,0xCA,0xC0,0xBD,0xE7])  # 你好世界
BIG5_BYTES = bytes([0xA7,0x41,0xA6,0x6E,0xB0,0xEA])

def rnd(r: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return r.randint(a, b)

def gen_utf8(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Start with BOM sometimes
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        parts.append(b"\xEF\xBB\xBF")
    # Add ASCII words and some multi-byte UTF-8 characters
    words = r.sample(ASCII_WORDS, k=rnd(r, 3, min(7, len(ASCII_WORDS))))
    parts.append(b" ".join(words))
    # Add some unicode punctuation / emojis
    uni_choices = [
        " – — ‘ ’ “ ” € © ™ ✓ αβγ 日本語 🚀",  # mixed
        "Привет мир", "Γειά σου Κόσμε", "مرحبا بالعالم",
    ]
    s = r.choice(uni_choices)
    parts.append(s.encode("utf-8", errors="strict"))
    # Optionally embed XML
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(b"\n" + r.choice(XML_SNIPPETS))
    return b"\n".join(parts)

def gen_utf16(r: random.Random, be: bool) -> bytes:
    text = gen_utf8(r).decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    enc = "utf-16-be" if be else "utf-16-le"
    data = text.encode(enc)
    # Add BOM sometimes, otherwise leave without
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        bom = b"\xFE\xFF" if be else b"\xFF\xFE"
        return bom + data
    return data

def gen_utf32(r: random.Random, be: bool) -> bytes:
    text = gen_utf8(r).decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    enc = "utf-32-be" if be else "utf-32-le"
    data = text.encode(enc)
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        bom = b"\x00\x00\xFE\xFF" if be else b"\xFF\xFE\x00\x00"
        return bom + data
    return data

def gen_legacy_blob(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    pool = [WIN1252_BYTES, ISO_8859_1_BYTES, SHIFT_JIS_BYTES, EUC_JP_BYTES, GBK_BYTES, BIG5_BYTES]
    parts = []
    # Prepend some ASCII/XML to help XML finders
    parts.append(r.choice(XML_SNIPPETS))
    # Mix several legacy chunks separated by spaces/newlines
    for _ in range(rnd(r, 1, 3)):
        parts.append(r.choice(pool))
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(b" \n ")
    return b"".join(parts)

def pad_or_trim(r: random.Random, data: bytes, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Optionally surround with random bytes to exercise size selection in stubs
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        pad_left = r.randbytes(rnd(r, 0, 8))
        pad_right = r.randbytes(rnd(r, 0, 8))
        data = pad_left + data + pad_right
    if len(data) > max_len:
        # Focus on start to keep BOMs if present
        data = data[:max_len]
    return data

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    choice = r.random()
    if choice < 0.35:
        data = gen_utf8(r)
    elif choice < 0.55:
        data = gen_utf16(r, be=bool(r.getrandbits(1)))
    elif choice < 0.70:
        data = gen_utf32(r, be=bool(r.getrandbits(1)))
    else:
        data = gen_legacy_blob(r)

    # Keep under limit and occasionally append extra ASCII to help decoders
    data = pad_or_trim(r, data, MAX_LEN)
    if r.random() < 0.3 and len(data) < MAX_LEN:
        tail = b"\n# end\n"
        data = (data + tail)[:MAX_LEN]
    return data
